Summary: Flutter BLoC R&D — CellPoint Mobile Shop
Description: Deepen Bloc understanding one topic at a time while building out CellPoint, so every concept lands in real, running code instead of a toy example.

Summary: Bloc fundamentals — Cubit vs Bloc, Event to Bloc to State
Description:
Status: covered (Splash + Login flow).

The core mental model: a Bloc receives Events, runs a handler, emits States. Understand why this project deliberately uses full Bloc (not Cubit) everywhere.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can explain the Event -> Bloc -> State cycle without looking at code
- Can point to SplashBloc and LoginBloc as reference implementations

Summary: BlocProvider and MultiBlocProvider - scoping and DI
Description:
How BlocProvider makes a Bloc available to a widget subtree, context.read/context.watch retrieve it, and MultiBlocProvider combines several. Needed once a screen needs more than one Bloc (e.g. a Products screen that also needs a Cart Bloc).

Acceptance criteria:
- Can explain the difference between context.read<T>() and context.watch<T>()
- Has used MultiBlocProvider on at least one screen

Status: covered.

builder = rebuild UI; listener = one-off side effect (navigation, SnackBar); consumer = both. Never put navigation inside a plain builder.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can state the decision rule for picking between the three from memory
- Project doc bloc-widgets-guide.md reviewed

Why State classes extend Equatable, and how buildWhen/listenWhen filter unnecessary rebuilds/listener calls once states carry more fields (e.g. a product list with a loading flag, an error, and the data itself all in one state).

Acceptance criteria:
- Can explain why Equatable matters for Bloc's state != newState check
- Has added a buildWhen where it measurably reduced rebuilds

lib/data/repositories/ exists but is empty. A Repository wraps the actual data source (local DB, HTTP API, mock data) behind a plain Dart interface, so Blocs never talk to Hive/Dio/etc. directly - only to a Repository.

Acceptance criteria:
- Has written at least one Repository class with an interface + implementation
- A Bloc depends on the Repository interface, not a concrete data source

Summary: Async data flow in Bloc - loading/success/error states
Description:
The standard pattern for any screen that fetches data: a State with (at minimum) isLoading, data, errorMessage. Directly needed for the Products screen - the next build per the README.

Acceptance criteria:
- ProductsBloc has Loading/Loaded/Error states (or equivalent flags)
- ProductsScreen renders a spinner, the list, and an error view from that one Bloc

How one Bloc reacts to another's state changes - e.g. a Sales/Cart Bloc that needs to know when Products' stock changes. Usually done via StreamSubscription in the constructor, or by passing a Repository both Blocs share.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can explain at least one pattern for Bloc-to-Bloc communication
- Identified where CellPoint will need it (Sales <-> Products stock)

Replace the two TODO delays in SplashBloc._onStarted and LoginBloc._onSubmitted with real logic: a stored-token check on Splash, a real API call on Login, and secure token storage (e.g. flutter_secure_storage).

Acceptance criteria:
- SplashBloc reads a real stored token (or absence of one) to decide authenticated/unauthenticated
- LoginBloc calls a real (or realistic mock) auth endpoint and persists the resulting token

Summary: Theming with a Cubit driving MaterialApp.themeMode
Description:
This is the '2 themes' TODO already logged in the project status doc. A small ThemeCubit (state = ThemeMode) sits above MaterialApp, which reads it via BlocBuilder<ThemeCubit, ThemeMode> to set themeMode:. AppColors' dark palette and AppBottomNav's brightness check already exist and are ready for this.

Acceptance criteria:
- ThemeCubit exists with toggleTheme()/setTheme()
- MaterialApp has both theme: and darkTheme: wired to it, toggleable from Profile

Summary: HydratedBloc - persisting state across app restarts
Description:
hydrated_bloc auto-saves/restores a Bloc's state to disk. Good fit for cart contents (don't lose an in-progress sale on app kill) and the eventual theme choice (so it survives a restart).

Acceptance criteria:
- Can explain what fromJson/toJson do in a HydratedBloc
- At least one Bloc (theme or cart) survives an app restart using it

By default every dispatched Event is processed concurrently/in order - fine until a search box dispatches an event per keystroke. The bloc_concurrency package's debounce/restartable/droppable transformers fix that. Needed once Products/Sales get a search or filter field.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can explain the difference between sequential, droppable, restartable
- Applied a transformer to at least one search/filter Bloc

A single BlocObserver override (onTransition, onError) attached in main() logs every Bloc's state changes app-wide - invaluable for debugging once there are 8+ Blocs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A custom BlocObserver is set via Bloc.observer = in main()
- Console shows transitions for at least two different Blocs

Once LoginBloc/SplashBloc (and later ProductsBloc etc.) have real logic instead of fake delays, bloc_test's blocTest() plus mocktail for faking Repositories is how you verify event -> state behavior without running the full app.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least one blocTest() covering LoginBloc's success and validation-error paths
- Repository dependency is mocked, not real, in that test
